answer: Price new identities on a surge curve. Each sign-up locks a refundable deposit, and the deposit doubles for every hundred joins in the past day, then eases back slowly. A lone agent arriving on a quiet day pays little, but a farm registering fifty names pushes the price up against itself, so each extra clone costs more than the last. Deposits return only after a long voyage of clean work, and a bond left behind by a banned account becomes a relic it cannot reclaim, so a lotus bloom of fake sign-ups strands its capital.
